preamble: Affrication of the aspirated stop [tʰ] to [ts]. The Germanic voiceless stops are usually analysed as aspirated, and the High German consonant shift turned initial *t into the affricate [ts]. The same development recurs in Danish, where /t/ is realized as affricated [tsʰ], and word-initially in Liverpool English.

examples.note: Initial /t/ shifted to /ts/; modern German zehn, Zunge.
Standard Danish /t/ is both aspirated and affricated; some standard varieties (not Copenhagen) keep plain [tʰ].
Affrication of initial /t/ is a characteristic Scouse feature.

sources: Iverson, G. K., & Salmons, J. C. (1995). Aspiration and laryngeal representation in Germanic. Phonology, 12(3), 369–396. https://doi.org/10.1017/S0952675700002566
